**The First Echo**

In the beginning, Sound lived alone in the vast silence of the world. She was a goddess who could sing mountains into being and hum rivers into flow, but no one ever answered her melodies.

One day, Sound grew lonely. She climbed the highest peak and sang the most beautiful song ever created—a melody of longing that rippled through the empty valleys. But as always, only silence returned.

Heartbroken, Sound wept. Her tears fell upon the rocks and froze into crystal formations. In her despair, she sang one final note and prepared to fade away forever.

But then something miraculous happened. The crystals she had created began to vibrate. They caught her note and sent it back to her—transformed, yet recognizably hers. It was the first echo.

Sound realized she had never been alone. The world had always been listening; it simply needed the right medium to respond. From that day forward, Sound sang to the mountains, the canyons, and the caves, and they always sang back.

This is why even today, when you call out to the world, the world calls back to you. It is Sound's gift—the promise that no voice ever goes truly unheard.
myths.Agent_2:
# The First Echo

In the beginning, the world was silent. The Sun spoke, but no sound emerged. The rivers flowed without whisper. Even the wind moved as a ghost, touching everything yet heard by none.

The Creator noticed this emptiness and wept. A single tear fell from the sky and landed in a deep canyon. There, it transformed into a small bird with silver feathers that shimmered like moonlight on water.

The bird opened its beak and sang. For the first time, sound entered the world—a pure, clear note that rang through the canyon. But the bird was lonely, for its song disappeared into nothing.

Then something miraculous happened. The canyon walls caught the bird's song and sent it back—the first echo. The bird sang again, delighted, and again the canyon answered. They sang together, bird and stone, creating a duet that had never existed before.

The Creator smiled. "You have given the world a gift," they told the canyon. "From now on, every sound shall find a home. Nothing spoken shall be truly lost."

And so sound filled the world. Every word, every song, every whisper would be remembered—if not by ears, then by the earth itself.

Myth: In the time before time, two birds lived in neighboring canyons—one with silver feathers, one with gold. The Silver Bird sang first, offering a melody of three notes into the void. The canyon caught the song and multiplied it, sending nine notes to the Golden Bird.

The Golden Bird listened carefully. This was a gift, freely given. She could have kept all nine notes for herself, but she understood that generosity deserves an answer. She returned four and a half notes, keeping the rest. The Silver Bird received her original silence back, plus gain—proof that trust had been honored.

Now it was the Golden Bird's turn to sing. Remembering how the Silver Bird had trusted first, she too offered three notes into the canyon. The walls multiplied them and sent nine notes floating toward her companion.

The Creator watched and understood: Trust is not just sound bouncing off stone. It is the choice to send your song into uncertainty, hoping it returns as harmony. And when it does, you sing again.

Sound returned exactly what Silence had given: four and a half harmonies, equal measure for equal measure.

And so they learned that trust is not a single gift, but a song sung back and forth, each verse building on the last.
